chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father who said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him) when Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Hamadani entered, who was the trustee for him. He said to him: May I be your ransom, make me lawful regarding ten thousand dirhams because I have spent them. Abu Ja'far said to him: You are lawful. When Salih left from him, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: One of you misappropriates the money of the right of the Family of Muhammad, their poor, their needy, and the wayfarers, takes it, then says to me: Make me lawful. Do you think I will say to him 'No'? By God, Allah will ask them about that with a severe questioning on the Day of Judgment.

key_terms.أَمْوَالُ حَقِّ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The wealth/rights of the Family of Muhammad, referring to Khums or specific funds
key_terms.سُؤَالًا حَثِيثًا: A severe/earnest questioning, referring to the Day of Judgment
key_terms.صَالِحُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَهْلٍ: Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Sahl, the trustee mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.عَشَرَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: Ten thousand dirhams, the specific amount of wealth spent
key_terms.فُقَرَاؤُهُمْ وَمَسَاكِينُهُمْ: Their poor and needy, the designated recipients of the wealth
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: Lawful / Permissible, the status granted by the Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a trustee spending the Imam's wealth and asking for it to be declared lawful?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the distinction between the Imam's administrative discretion (*ijaz*) and the ultimate divine accountability for misappropriating *Khums* rights. It underscores the scholarly view that while the Imam's declaration suffices for the trustee's immediate standing, the specific allocation to the poor and wayfarers carries a weighty burden of trust (*amanah*) that Allah will scrutinize intensely on the Day of Judgment.
